We have been bullish on Bitcoin since October 2023 (+225% since then).


Dear Timothy,

Crypto is going moon… AGAIN.

Since Election Day, almost $1 TRILLION has been added to global crypto market cap. We’ve been riding that wave higher with our subscribers. In fact, we have been bullish on Bitcoin since October 2023 (+225% since then).

We’ve got a complete Crypto update (and more) in this edition of Weekend Reading. Before we get to that, here are this week’s quick links:

[WATCH]  Navigating the New Market Reality: Jim Rickards 1-on-1 w/ Keith McCullough
https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/ol-type-macro2Cmarket-insights/2sn1tjy/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

[WATCH]  David Salem Explores the Fed’s Dilemma, China’s Investment Trap, and 'Rational Exuberance' in Markets

[ADD TO CALENDAR] Digital Assets Playbook: Crypto Just Went MOON… What Comes Next?
https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/l-764243-2024-11-22-2sn1qxc/2sn1tk5/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

Let’s get into it.

As crypto ripped higher this week, we began to question our long Bitcoin thesis when we learned the most reliable contraindicator of all time, CNBC’s Jim Cramer, said he’s now bullish on it. LOL.

“All I can tell you is, own Bitcoin. That’s a winner,” Cramer said.

Jim is obviously a donkey. If you recall, this is the guy who said, “Bear Stearns is fine. Do not take your money out” in March of 2008. Five days later, the firm was mercy folded into JPMorgan Chase (read: bailed out) at $2 per share.

Jim also said of Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes, "It's reasonable to compare you to Steve Jobs.” Not to beat a dead horse, but Jim also called imprisoned fraudster and FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried the "new JP Morgan."

You get the point. Given Jim’s track record, his about-face on Bitcoin was disconcerting.

Still, we’re pleased Jim is finally joining the Bitcoin party, even if he’s missed the +225% move Hedgeye subscribers have been riding since our signal went bullish on Bitcoin in October 2023.

Our Bitcoin track record is clear – we’re right far more often than we’re wrong.

	BULLISH (April 2020 – May 2021): +519%  

	BEARISH (May 2021 – July 2021): +10% 

	BULLISH (August 2021 – December 2021): +10%  

	BEARISH (December 2021 – October 2023): -43% 

	BULLISH (October 2023 – Present): +225% 

If you want money-making ideas to take advantage of the move in crypto, we’ve got something special planned for you.

Join Hedgeye Digital Assets analysts Josh Steiner, Christian Drake, and Ishmael Asad for a special Crypto webcast on Tuesday, November 26th at 11:00am ET. 

“Digital Assets Playbook: Crypto Just Went MOON… What Comes Next?”
https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/l-764243-2024-11-22-2sn1qxc/2sn1tk5/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

Josh, Christian and Ishmael will unpack everything you need to know to confidently allocate your capital during this historic Crypto bull run.

Just consider the following…

	SEC Chair Gensler to depart agency on January 20, a victory for the more than 50 million Americans who own crypto.
	The cryptocurrency industry's leading super PACs put $134 million into congressional races this election cycle – helping to elect 276 pro-crypto candidates in the House and 20 in the Senate.
	Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase COIN has rocketed up the top of App store rankings. From 458th most popular app on November 4th to 42nd most popular app recently.
	The US Government's 203,000 Bitcoin are now valued at $20 billion. And President Elect Donald Trump suggested he might even create a strategic Bitcoin reserve.
	Total government Bitcoin holdings around the world control ~$50 billion worth of the cryptocurrency.
	Institutional investors own $227 billion worth of Bitcoin (or 11.6% of the total supply).

So yes, there’s a lot to discuss! 😉

By the way, want more crypto long ideas? Learn about the 3 other Best Idea Long Ideas our Digital Assets team likes with a Digital Assets Pro subscription.
https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/pecial-digital-assets-pro-1203/2sn1tk8/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

How about Macro?

Our veteran Director of Capital Allocation David Salem recently appeared on Bloomberg Surveillance with Tom Keene to discuss Hedgeye's market outlook under the incoming Trump administration, the future of the Federal Reserve, inflation, and more.

“I think the Fed ought to be very, very careful about cutting rates too quickly,” David told Tom. “It's going to be very difficult for the Fed to move this gigantic supertanker called the 'U.S. Economy' towards inflation anything close to their 2% target over the next year. And that suggests that they ought to be very measured and patient in further reductions of the policy rate.”

Watch the entire interview here: https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/rg-type-macro2Cmarket-insights/2sn1tk2/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

In other words, be careful of inflation rearing its ugly head. Our inflation outlook isn’t just U.S. centric either.

We see stagflation impacting global growth throughout the first half of 2025. As CEO Keith McCullough wrote this week, “That means #HFL (higher for longer) on not only US Inflation’s ROC (rate of change), but the world’s.”

If you want a “Stagflation Survival Guide” to help you navigate your portfolio through the coming market risks, we’ve got you covered there too. Our Elite Macro subscription  has everything you need to confidently risk manage the next 3-6 months of stagflation. We’re also running our “best deal all year” on Elite Macro so there’s that.
https://info.hedgeye.com/e/764243/ELM-500-1999Y-elite-macro-1255/2sn1tkc/1875524236/h/Wl3X0yool7BH-E5vE8qWOBXnZROnRZxIicaIsKnbJts

Finally, Keith’s conversation with market commentator, author and iconoclast Jim Rickards is definitely worth your time this weekend.

"AI is not your friend," Jim Rickards explained in this conversation with Keith. Jim continues…

"The machines are definitely smart enough. I mean, people have Alexa, Siri on the dashboard, your iPhone, Alexa's in your house, you know, "Alexa, turn down the lights." When you do the deep dive in artificial intelligence and you're into layers and nodes and edges and weights and all the things that actually go into it, I built AI systems, it's all math. But it's not your friend. But we tend to give it these human attributes. the same thing applies in, well, I make the point in the book, in the stock market, nuclear war fighting, etc., we tend to trust the system when we shouldn't trust it. You have to understand how it actually works."

This is a wide-ranging and thought-provoking conversation. Worth a listen this weekend.

- The Hedgeye Team

Josh Steiner: If you look at the last 25 years in the U.S., you can track M2, which is a pretty decent measure of the money supply.

Money supply at the end of 1999 was $4.7 trillion. As of the late September update, M2 had risen from $4.7 trillion to $21.2 trillion. When you do the math on that, it works out to $1 being worth 77.8% less today versus where it was at the end of 1999, simply because the number of dollars in circulation has increased by 450%.

Steiner: The other way to think about that is the pace at which you’re devaluing the dollar over time. In the last 25 years, the annualize rate of debasement is 6.26%. It’s obviously not in a straight line, although up until 2020 it was fairly consistent. The M2 growth rate ranged from 5% to a high of 10% during periods of recession.

We got into a very aggressive period of monetary expansion during the pandemic where the growth in M2 was north of 25% year-over-year.

Even using the BLS’s more forgiving CPI measure, the Dollar has lost about 53% of its purchasing power since 1999.

Now let’s look at the hedges out there. Gold, since 1999, is up +10.4% on a compound annual growth rate basis. That’s quite a bit better when compared with M2’s +6.26% compound annual growth rate for debasing the U.S. Dollar. This is obviously a fortuitous time to be getting into Gold.

The next slide is equities. A somewhat inauspicious time to get into equities, in 1999, but nevertheless equities are up +5.6% on a compound annual growth rate basis. Again, that compares to M2’s +6.26% debasement.

What about Real Estate, a big hard asset class? Single family residential property is up +4.9% per year compounded since the end of 1999. Again, relative to that +6.26% monetary debasement.

So what we did next was go back even further, to when the U.S. came off the Gold Standard in 1968, and indexing these different asset classes to 100 in 1968.

The black dash line is money supply or M2. Using round numbers, it has risen 40-fold. So, there is 40 times as much money in the system today relative to when we came off the Gold Standard in 1968.

The gold line represents Gold. How about that asset? Gold has risen 66-fold over that time.

The S&P 500 has risen 58-fold as the increase there.

And finally, the green line is property, up 19-fold.

What I would have you take away from this is that financial assets and hard assets don’t outperform inflation, not when you regard inflation as the money supply. They simply track it over time. They can dislocate to the upside and downside. You can see that in Gold in 1980. If you bought Gold in 1980, for instance, you had a really lousy investment for the next two decades. If you bought equities in 1999, you had a really lousy investment for quite a while as well.

The point is, over time however, these things just track the amount of money in the system. So as the money supply grows, in order to avoid debasement in your purchasing power, you need to own hard assets or financial assets, so things like Real Estate, Gold or Equities…

Steiner: Why does this matter today?

Well, from 2008 to 2023, we went from 35% debt-to-GDP to 100%. The projection over the next 35 years is that we’re going to go from 100% to 170%.

These projections from the CBO have a really good track record of being wrong. Wrong in the sense that they underestimate what debt-to-GDP ratios end up being. We’re obviously on a really unsustainable path. If we don’t fix this, we’re going to have to print an extraordinary amount of money in order to be able to monetize the debt that’s going to need to be issued and sold in order to fund all these obligations.
